module_title: Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP - Part IV) - Basic Understanding
introduction: Part IV of the Constitution (Articles 36 to 51) contains the 'Directive Principles of State Policy' (DPSP). These principles serve as guidelines or directives that the state (government) should keep in mind while formulating policies and enacting laws. Their primary aim is to establish a 'Welfare State' in India.

core_concepts.title: Source
core_concepts.description: The concept of DPSP was borrowed from the Constitution of Ireland (which had copied it from the Spanish Constitution).

core_concepts.title: Nature: Non-Justiciable
core_concepts.description: Unlike Fundamental Rights, DPSPs are non-justiciable. This means that if the government fails to implement them, you cannot approach a court of law to force their implementation.

core_concepts.title: Objective
core_concepts.description: While Fundamental Rights aim to establish 'Political Democracy', the primary objective of DPSPs is to establish 'Social and Economic Democracy' in the country.

core_concepts.title: Significance of Article 37
core_concepts.description: Article 37 explicitly states that although these principles are not enforceable by any court, they are nevertheless 'fundamental in the governance of the country' and it shall be the duty of the State to apply them in making laws.

important_entities.name: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
important_entities.significance: He described the Directive Principles as a 'Novel Feature' of the Indian Constitution.

important_entities.name: Granville Austin
important_entities.significance: He described the Directive Principles and the Fundamental Rights together as the 'Conscience of the Constitution'.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often confuse the nature of FRs and DPSPs. Remember: Fundamental Rights (FRs) are Enforceable (Justiciable) in courts, whereas DPSPs are Non-Enforceable (Non-Justiciable).

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: IRE-land has 4 letters (well, almost, think 'Eire' has 4)
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: A common memory hook: DPSP is in Part 4 (IV) and was borrowed from Ireland.

exam_strategy_tips: Questions asking which country DPSP was borrowed from (Ireland) and which part it belongs to (Part IV, Arts 36-51) appear in almost every basic competitive exam.
The concept of a 'Welfare State' is enshrined in which part of the Constitution? (Answer: Directive Principles of State Policy).
